entities.summary: Sthennis was a renowned Olynthian sculptor from the 4th century BC, known for his contributions to the development of classical Greek art. Born in Olynthos, Thessaly, Greece, Sthennis was the son of Herodotus, a celebrated historian, and father of Herodorus, a sculptor in his own right. Sthennis' works, including the iconic statue of Apollo, have been lost to time, leaving behind only fragmented descriptions and references in ancient texts. Despite this, his impact on the art world can still be felt today, with many of his contemporaries and successors paying homage to his innovative techniques and mastery of the craft. As a sculptor, Sthennis was part of a broader cultural movement that sought to revive and celebrate the artistic traditions of ancient Greece. He was particularly influential in the development of the 'Olynthian style,' a distinctive approach to sculpture characterized by its use of contrapposto and the depiction of mythological subjects. Sthennis' legacy extends beyond his artistic achievements, as he was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of the city of Olynthos, which was a major center of culture and learning in the ancient Greek world. Through his support of the arts, Sthennis helped to promote the values of creativity, intellectual curiosity, and cultural exchange that would become hallmarks of the ancient Greek city-state. As such, Sthennis plays an important role in the history of art and culture, serving as a testament to the enduring power of human creativity and the importance of preserving and celebrating our shared cultural heritage.
